campaigns.title: Does the concave engine work end-to-end?
campaigns.question: Do concave compound pieces run through the full pipeline (engine, runner, ledger, projections) producing valid, overlap-free packings, and does the convex control behave as in the parent project?
campaigns.hypothesis: All runs complete without error; every best legalised packing verifies overlap-free and contained by the independent checker; on the squ-in-squ n=6 convex control, harden's best legalised size is <= rigid's (the parent project found hardening wins on squares in a square). Concave instances are smoke runs only: no scientific claim is made from them here.
campaigns.decision_rule: Pass iff (a) zero run errors across all cells, (b) scripts/verify_packings.js reports zero pairwise overlaps (tolerance 1e-9) and full container containment on the best packing of every cell, and (c) the convex control holds: harden best_L <= rigid best_L on squ-in-squ n=6. Any failure is fixed in the engine, recorded as a plan amendment, and the campaign re-runs from scratch.
campaigns.decision: Pass per the pre-registered decision rule: (a) 0 run errors, (b) verifier reports 0 failures on 12 best packings, (c) convex control holds (harden 3.0000 <= rigid 3.0000 on squ-in-squ n=6). Pipeline validated; proceeding to C01 concave pilot.

campaigns.title: Concave pilot: does hardening beat rigid starts on concave pieces?
campaigns.question: On three concave families at small n, does harden reach smaller containers than rigid starts at matched budget, and do the convex controls behave as in the parent project?
campaigns.hypothesis: Two-factor hypothesis: hardening beats rigid starts on concave families. (1) Path length: inscribed-disk share of piece area is ltri 6%, cross 31%, star5 41%, far below any convex piece (square 79%, triangle 61%, pentagon 86%), so the morph has far more room to work. (2) Hidden interlocking optima: concave optima require orientations a rigid search cannot easily reach. Positive control squ-in-squ (hardening wins in the parent project) should replicate; negative control tri-in-squ (tessellates) should tie or favour rigid.
campaigns.decision_rule: Descriptive pilot; no confirmatory claim. Report per-family harden vs rigid exact two-sided sign tests (best legalised size per instance, relative tol 1e-9). Proceed to C02 (pre-registered flagship: 48 seeds, frozen settings, harden/rigid/sa/pc) if (i) harden wins >= rigid losses on concave families overall, and (ii) the positive control replicates qualitatively (harden >= rigid on squ-in-squ). If harden is systematically worse everywhere including the positive control, the method params do not transfer to this codebase state: run a concave tuning campaign before C02 and record it as an amendment here.
campaigns.decision: Per the decision rule: (i) fails on strict counts (7 wins < 10 losses) and is a dead tie (5 vs 5) at noise-robust tolerance; (ii) positive control does not replicate at 16 seeds. Do NOT proceed to C02 flagship as designed. Next: targeted engine-replication check (squ-in-squ n=11, 32 seeds) plus a mechanism campaign (checkpoint-handoff on ltri n=5) to test whether the morph delivers the system into basins rigid search cannot reach - the instance-level story the pilot actually supports.

campaigns.title: Engine replication (squ n=11, 32 seeds) + handoff baselines
campaigns.question: Does the generalized engine reproduce the parent's squ-in-squ n=11 signature, and what are fresh harden baselines on the handoff instances?
campaigns.hypothesis: The generalized engine reproduces the parent project's signature result: with 32 runs at budget 1, harden reaches Trump's n=11 record (3.87708359) while rigid does not. (C01's 16-seed control could not test this: the tilted basin is a rare event.) Fresh harden baselines on ltri n=5 and star5 n=9 supply checkpoints for the handoff test.
campaigns.decision_rule: Replication passes iff harden best-of-32 <= 3.87709 (Trump's record 3.87708359 + 1e-5) AND harden best < rigid best - 1e-3 on squ-in-squ n=11. If replication fails, halt: do not interpret any handoff results until the engine difference is found. If it passes, the ltri n=5 and star5 n=9 harden runs supply the checkpoints for C02b-ltri and C02b-star5.
campaigns.decision: Replication passes per the pre-registered rule (harden 3.87708674 <= 3.87709 and < rigid - 1e-3). Engine validated; C02b handoff launches with checkpoints extracted from these harden replays.

campaigns.title: Checkpoint handoff: ltri n=5
campaigns.question: Does rigid search reach harden's ltri n=5 pinwheel basin when started from a mid-morph checkpoint?
campaigns.hypothesis: On ltri-in-squ n=5, where harden beat rigid by 0.61 in C01, rigid search started from harden's tau~0.5 checkpoint reaches harden's basin (L≈4.0) while rigid from random starts does not. This is a mechanism test, not an efficiency test: the checkpoint cost a harden run, which is beside the point - the question is WHERE the search goes.
campaigns.decision_rule: Handoff succeeds iff rigid-from-checkpoint best-of-16 <= (C02a harden best on ltri n=5) + 1e-3 AND rigid-from-random best-of-16 > (C02a harden best) + 0.01. Success means the morph's contribution on this instance is basin delivery: rigid search reaches the pinwheel once started in its neighborhood but not from random starts. Failure (checkpoint cannot reach it either) means the late morph does essential work beyond basin delivery, or the checkpoint choice (tau~0.5) was wrong - either way the mechanism is not basin delivery alone.
campaigns.decision: Handoff succeeds per the pre-registered rule. Basin delivery confirmed on ltri n=5.

campaigns.title: Checkpoint handoff: star5 n=9
campaigns.question: Does rigid search reach harden's star5 n=9 basin when started from a mid-morph checkpoint?
campaigns.hypothesis: On star5-in-squ n=9, where harden beat rigid by 0.10 in C01, rigid search started from harden's tau~0.5 checkpoint reaches harden's basin while rigid from random starts does not. Mechanism test, not efficiency test.
campaigns.decision_rule: Handoff succeeds iff rigid-from-checkpoint best-of-16 <= (C02a harden best on star5 n=9) + 1e-3 AND rigid-from-random best-of-16 > (C02a harden best) + 0.01. Same interpretation as C02b-ltri.
campaigns.decision: Handoff succeeds per the pre-registered rule. Basin delivery confirmed on star5 n=9.

campaigns.title: Morph-fraction ablation on ltri n=5
campaigns.question: How much of the morph path is needed to reach the ltri n=5 pinwheel basin?
campaigns.hypothesis: harden-half (tau0=0.5) reaches the ltri n=5 pinwheel (L<=4.001) but harden-quarter (tau0=0.25) does not: the basin is found in the first half of the morph, consistent with the tau~0.5 checkpoint handoff.
campaigns.decision_rule: Compare best-of-16 legalised sizes. If harden-half reaches <= 4.001 while harden-quarter does not (gap > 0.01), the basin is found in the first half of the morph. If both reach it, even a quarter-morph suffices and the critical interval is tau in [0, 0.25]. If neither reaches it, the full morph path is needed and the checkpoint result (tau~0.5) stands as the localization. Descriptive; feeds the mechanism story, no confirmatory claim.
campaigns.decision: Both half and quarter morphs reach the pinwheel: critical interval is tau in [0,0.25].

campaigns.title: Convex rare-event sweep at n=11
campaigns.question: Does the n=11 hardening signature generalize across convex shapes?
campaigns.hypothesis: The n=11 rare-event signature (harden reaches the record, rigid does not) is square-specific: present for squ-in-squ, absent for tri/pen/hex. Null (all four show it) is equally reportable.
campaigns.decision_rule: Per family: 'signature present' iff harden best-of-32 <= record + 1e-3 AND rigid best-of-32 > record + 1e-3 (record from catalog; pen/hex records as listed). Report exact bests regardless. This is the generalization test of the parent's n=11 finding.
campaigns.decision: Signature present for squ and tri; pen ties; hex favors rigid. Square-specific hypothesis rejected.

campaigns.title: Morph-part factorial on concave instances
campaigns.question: Which part of the methodology matters, for which concave shapes?
campaigns.hypothesis: The C03 localization generalizes: on concave instances the compress phase contributes nothing (nocompress ~= harden) and a quarter-morph suffices; rigid trails on the instances where C01 found harden wins.
campaigns.decision_rule: Per instance, rank the 5 methods by best-of-16 at 1e-4. Pre-registered hypothesis: on concave instances, harden-nocompress is within 1e-3 of harden on >=5/7 instances (the disk-compress phase is unnecessary, per C03's ltri result). Also report, per instance, the minimal morph in {quarter, half, full} reaching within 1e-3 of the instance best (descriptive companion to the meta-analysis).
campaigns.decision: Nocompress hypothesis rejected; compress phase essential, short morph suffices.

campaigns.title: Pentagons in a pentagon
campaigns.question: Does the hardening effect survive a change of container shape?
campaigns.hypothesis: Two-sided scoping: container shape interacts with the hardening effect. If pen-in-pen shows harden wins where pen-in-squ did not (C15: 1 vs 8), the container - not just the piece - belongs in the predictor set.
campaigns.decision_rule: Instance-level reporting (best-of-16 harden vs rigid at 1e-4); sign test across the 4 instances is descriptive only (n=4 is underpowered by design - this is a scoping campaign for the container axis). No external records exist for pen-in-pen; all comparisons are relative.
campaigns.decision: All ties; no hardening advantage for pentagons in pentagons.

campaigns.title: Concave n-scaling
campaigns.question: Does the hardening advantage grow with n?
campaigns.hypothesis: The harden advantage grows with piece count within concave families (more pieces -> more interlocking -> more steric barriers for rigid search).
campaigns.decision_rule: Per family, Cochran-Armitage-style trend: pre-registered one-sided test of whether P(harden beats rigid at 1e-4) increases with n across the pooled instances (C01 n=5..8 + C02a + C07 n=9..11 for that family). Report per-instance bests and gaps regardless.

findings.text: C00: concave compound pieces run end-to-end. 48 runs, 0 errors; the independent verifier reports 0 overlaps and full containment on all 12 best packings; the convex control holds (harden best_L 3.0000 <= rigid 3.0000 on squ-in-squ n=6). The generalized engine is bit-identical to the parent engine on convex families (5/5 differential cases), agrees with brute-force overlap on 1200/1200 concave configurations, and passes a finite-difference gradient check at 8.47e-11.

C01 concave pilot (1600 runs, 0 errors, 100/100 best packings verified overlap-free): the strong two-factor prediction is NOT supported. At tie tolerance 1e-4, concave harden vs rigid is 5 vs 5 with 7 ties (p=1); strict 1e-9 counts (7 vs 10) are inflated by 1e-6 legalization noise visible on squ-in-squ controls. The effect is instance-heterogeneous, not family-level: harden wins decisively on ltri n=5 (+0.61, 13%) and n=6 (+0.03), star5 n=7 (+0.011), n=8 (+0.033), n=9 (+0.10); rigid wins decisively on ltri n=7 (-0.27), n=8 (-0.10), cross n=5 (-0.33), n=8 (-0.18). Orientation variance of best rigid packings correlates only 0.27 with harden advantage - no clean geometric predictor emerges. harden crushes the classical baselines on concave: vs sa 19-6 (p=0.015), vs pc 24-1 (p=1.5e-6). Positive control (squ-in-squ) did not replicate the parent's n=11 signature at 16 seeds - likely a power issue (parent used 32 runs for a rare tilted-basin event), to be checked by a targeted replication.

C02a replication PASSES: the generalized engine reproduces the parent's signature - squ-in-squ n=11 harden best-of-32 = 3.87708674 (Trump's record 3.87708359 + 3.2e-6) vs rigid best 3.88826742. Fresh baselines: ltri n=5 harden 4.00000061 vs rigid 4.61096103; star5 n=9 harden 4.57295043 vs rigid 4.67261308. 128 runs, 0 errors, 6/6 best packings verified. Proceeding to C02b handoff as pre-registered.

C02b-ltri handoff SUCCEEDS: rigid-from-checkpoint best-of-16 = 4.000000 (all 16 runs hit the pinwheel, median 4.000000) vs rigid-from-random best-of-16 = 4.747547 (median 5.000001). Decision rule met: checkpoint <= harden best (4.00000061) + 1e-3 and random > harden best + 0.01. The morph's contribution on ltri n=5 is basin delivery: rigid search reaches the pinwheel from the tau~0.5 neighborhood but not from random starts. 32 runs, 0 errors, 17/17 best packings verified.

C03 ablation: BOTH harden-half (best 4.000000) and harden-quarter (best 4.000001) reach the ltri n=5 pinwheel; rigid best 4.610961. Per the pre-registered rule, the critical interval is tau in [0, 0.25]: even a small amount of corner rounding (tau0=0.25) suffices for the compress phase to find the pinwheel positions, and the short remaining morph grows the corners in. The disk phase is not necessary. 48 runs, 0 errors, 3/3 best packings verified.

C02b-star5 handoff SUCCEEDS: rigid-from-checkpoint best-of-16 = 4.572969 (within 1.9e-5 of C02a harden best 4.57295043; median 4.655183) vs rigid-from-random best-of-16 = 4.684325 (median 4.858657). Decision rule met on both clauses. Basin delivery confirmed on a second concave family: rigid search reaches harden's basin from the tau~0.5 neighborhood but not from random starts. 32 unique runs (worker races produced duplicate rows, deduped by id), 0 errors, 17/17 best packings verified.

C04: the n=11 signature is NOT square-specific. squ-in-squ: harden 3.877087 reaches Trump's record, rigid 3.888267 does not (signature present). tri-in-squ: harden 2.490961 vs record 2.49, rigid 2.500019 (signature present). pen-in-squ: harden 5.115946 vs rigid 5.115562, both within 4e-4 of Friedman's 5.11555 record - a tie, no signature. hex-in-squ: rigid 6.332907 beats harden 6.339748 and sits nearer the 6.33218 record - a rigid win. The pre-registered square-specific hypothesis is rejected; the pattern now needs the meta-analysis (disk_share/symmetry as candidate moderators). 256 runs, 0 errors, 8/8 verified.

C06 pen-in-pen: all four instances (n=5..8) are ties between harden and rigid at 1e-4 (identical bests: 2.618034, 2.618034, 3.078690, 3.335175). No hardening advantage for pentagons in a pentagonal container at these n - consistent with the parent's C15 (pentagons in a square: 1 vs 8) and with C04's pen-in-squ n=11 tie. Pentagons look like a shape where the effect is absent regardless of container. 128 runs, 0 errors, 8/8 best packings verified with the fixed pentagon tightContainer branch.

C05 REJECTS the pre-registered nocompress hypothesis (2/7 instances, needed >=5): harden-nocompress usually fails badly (ltri n=5: 4.6213 vs harden 4.0000). Correction to the C03 reading: the COMPRESS phase is essential - C03's harden-quarter still had a compress phase (at tau=0.25). What the data now say: (a) a soft compress phase is required to arrange positions; (b) the morph may start nearly rigid (tau0=0.25 suffices on 4/7: ltri 5,6, star5 7,9); (c) the full disk-to-shape morph is overkill. Surprises: on cross n=5 the full morph HURTS (harden 6.6569 vs half/quarter/nocompress/rigid all 6.3246); on star5 n=8 only the full morph reaches 4.4173. 560 runs, 0 errors, 35/35 verified.

C07: no clean monotonic trend of harden advantage with n. ltri: ties at n=9,10 (6.0), harden wins big at n=11 (6.5769 vs 7.0). cross: tie at n=9, rigid wins n=10 (8.7089 vs 8.8375) and n=11 (9.1924 vs 9.3279). star5: rigid n=10 by 0.007, harden n=11 by 0.011. The pre-registered trend test goes to the meta-analysis pooled with C01/C02a. 256 runs, 0 errors, 16/16 verified.

META-ANALYSIS (pre-registered): no tested predictor survives. 37 instances, 9 harden-win events. H1 concavity: 7/22 concave vs 2/15 convex, one-sided Fisher p=0.187, fail to reject. H2 n-trend within concave: ltri Z=-0.76 p=0.78, star5 Z=1.15 p=0.126, pooled Z=0.49 p=0.31, fail to reject. H3 disk_share: medians both 0.408, one-sided Mann-Whitney p=0.149, fail to reject. Mixed-effects logistic (7 fixed + family random intercept on 37 obs/9 events) is overparameterized: family-level covariates compete with the random intercept (family_sd collapses to ~0 with huge uncertainty) and VB intervals are implausibly tight - reported as unstable per the plan's contingency. Sensitivity: pooled-duplicate resolution changes 0/37 outcomes. Correction recorded: the frozen plan misremembered C01's design (actual: ltri 5-10, cross 4-8, star5 5-10, squ 8-12, tri 8-10); inclusion corrected to the real design, intent unchanged. Headline: hardening wins are real (9/37, incl. replicated n=11 signatures and the ltri pinwheel) but NOT predicted by concavity, piece count trend, or disk share. Events cluster in ltri (3/7) and star5 (4/7); cross is 0/8 despite being concave.
